messages:
morgan: Heads-up — discovered a regression hitting Mixtral/Qwen paths when head-dim is not 8/16 aligned. FlashAttention tries to run, detects mask/head-slab misalignment, and we silently fallback to SDPA/Triton. Results: corrupted incremental KV offsets + 2.3x p99 on long-context workloads.

lee: ugh. do you have a quick repro?

morgan: repro is small. run: `./bench_infer --model mixtral-7b --bs 1 --seq 2048 --head-dim 14 --kernel auto --use-kv-cache`. Flash logs show fallback. snippet:```
[INFO] kernel_selector: trying flashattention
[WARN] flash: mask_stride != expected_stride -> fallback
[INFO] runtime: using sdpa_triton_fallback
[ERROR] kvcache: write_offset mismatch (expected 0x7ff, got 0x7f3)
```

anya: is the corruption coming from how we compute prefix_offsets for uneven head slabs?

morgan: looks like it. Flash path assumes contiguous head slab layout multiple-of-8 for the mask buffer. When head-dim = 14 we allocated mask bytes differently; Triton path pads but our KV write path didn't account for the pad, so offsets slide.

sam: any perf numbers comparing flash vs sdpa fallback?

morgan: yes. measured on p4d-ish machine:
- flash (aligned head-dim 16): p50 45ms, p95 78ms, p99 120ms
- fallback (head-dim 14 -> SDPA/Triton): p50 82ms, p95 185ms, p99 275ms (2.3x p99 reg)
Throughput drops ~40% for long seqs due to slower GEMM/transpose and extra memcpy.

zane: interesting — also affects KV caching because the KV buffer copy uses computed kv_stride = head_dim/8 * 128 or something. If head_dim odd multiple we end up with floor division mismatch.

anya: can we short-term force kernel selection to skip flash for non-8-aligned head dims? Safer but loses perf on models like Mixtral with 14/38 head dims.

lee: yeah that's the tactical fix: select `sdpa_triton` for non-8/16 head dims until we patch mask handling. But long-term we should either pad mask layout or adjust KV write/read to include mask padding.

morgan: agreed. I prototyped two patches: (A) head-pad shim at runtime (pad head_dim up to 16 before kernel selection, hide padding in blob metadata), (B) fix KV copy math to use explicit mask_stride computed from kernel choice. Patch A gives immediate perf win (restores flash in most cases) but adds complexity to model metadata. Patch B cleaner but touches hot path.

sam: any correctness risks for patch A? If we pad logically but keep actual weights contiguous it might break any model that relies on exact head_dim?

morgan: we only pad ephemeral buffers (mask, kv stride) at runtime, not model weights. We insert zero-pad in mask and round up head stride for allocation. Need tests to ensure logits/attention scores unchanged.

zane: also check RoPE scaling math — some models (Qwen variants) have RoPE scaling that depends on head width; padding could alter rotary frequency alignment.

morgan: good catch. I ran the eval suite on unit prompts — logits identical to 1e-6 with pad for most models, but Qwen-rope variants show tiny drift at long contexts. Not catastrophic but needs explicit gating per model.

anya: plan then:
- short-term: add runtime guard to avoid Flash for known problematic head dims OR enable pad shim only for models where we've validated rope invariance.
- medium: implement KV copy math fix that computes strides from kernel selection and add alignment-aware memcpy.
- tests: add regression test in perf harness that runs mixtral/qwen head-dim combos with kv caching and compares outputs.

devops-bot: CI job #4218 started: runtime-integration/mixtral-headpad (canary).

morgan: created RFC PR: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pulls/3467 — contains bench results, proposed patches A/B, and perf graphs. Please review.

lee: I'll pick up the KV-stride fix (B) and write unit for kvcache copy stride. Assigning to me.

sam: I'll add a canary rollout plan for the runtime guard + metric alerts (p99, error-count, kv-offset-errors).

zane: I'll run evals for RoPE invariance on Qwen variants and post numbers.

ci-bot: CI #4218 finished: 3 failures (two flaky tests, one expected diff in qwen-rope-eval).

morgan: noted. Created a short-term rollback flag so we can disable pad shim by env var. Putting patch into canary after fixes to kvcache.

anya: sounds good. Add a high-level note in the incidents channel if canary shows >1.5x p99 increase.

morgan: will do. Action items: Lee -> kvcache stride patch, Zane -> rope evals, Sam -> canary + alerts, Morgan -> PR updates and canary.

lee: ack. starting on kvcache patch now.

sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
